title: Dedicated intake: throughput guardrails & scaling patterns for enterprise SLA triage
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a pragmatic triage rubric and intake checklist specifically for enterprise Dedicated capacity requests focused on guaranteed throughput and scaling behavior. Current intake forms surface requested throughput and GPU family but lack consistent rules for burst-to-reserved ratios, tail-latency targets, preemption risk, and network/egress constraints. This ticket teams PM + Eng + Solutions to define guardrails that streamline intake, speed decisioning, and produce deterministic commitments for sales/concsierge.
acceptance_criteria: An intake checklist (one-page) that surface: steady-state TPS, expected token/sec per request, p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency SLOs, expected burst multiplier and burst duration, GPU family constraints, expected model footprint and KV-cache needs, and isolation/security requirements.

A triage rubric that maps intake answers to one of: 'Self-serve (hosted)', 'Dedicated - Standard SLA', 'Dedicated - High SLA (reserved high-priority)', or 'Private deployment required', with explicit thresholds.
Engineering-owned scaling patterns documented: warm-pool sizing formula, cold-start mitigation, autoscaling cooldowns, and explicit preemption/burst policies.
A short playbook for sales/solutions with templated responses for common SLA asks and an estimated lead time table by GPU class.
Pilot review completed with 2 enterprise customers and adjustments captured in this ticket's comments.
decisions: Use p99.9 as the default tail SLO for enterprise high-SLA triage, with P99 used for standard reserved tiers.
Burst-to-reserved ratio will be expressed as: allowed_burst_tokens_per_minute : reserved_tokens_per_minute; default max burst multiplier = 4x for GPUs with fast preemption handling, 2x otherwise.
GPU family classification for intake will be simplified to: 'A-Class (latest), B-Class (balanced), C-Class (cost-optimized)'. Exact SKU mapping maintained in an engineering reference doc.
For requests requiring encrypted KMS-backed keys or air-gapped deployment, route directly to 'Private deployment' and start enterprise onboarding flow.
notes: Context: multiple enterprise deals stalled >2 weeks while infra triaged unclear throughput asks; sales needs deterministic answers within 24-48h.
We must avoid commitments that rely on optimistic caching; intake should require a small representative latency/throughput test where possible (synthetic load or customer-provided traces).
Trade-offs: tighter SLAs reduce platform packing efficiency; guardrails should favor predictable SLAs with optional paid burst capacity rather than uncontrolled bursts.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Asha Patel: Initial ticket created after intake sync with GTM. Captured ask: customers want explicit guarantees for reserved throughput and predictable burst behaviour. Blocking point: currently engineering needs standardized metrics to size pools.

2025-02-14 - Daniel Kim: Eng triage meeting notes: proposed metrics to require on intake: average tokens/sec per request, concurrency distribution (p50/p95), and anticipated session length. Engineering will prototype a sizing formula based on measured per-token GPU throughput for quantized models.

2025-02-18 - Ravi Singh (ENG): Added risk note: certain older GPU families have >3s cold start for large KV caches; recommend disallowing >2s cold start requirement on those SKUs or requiring pre-warmed nodes.
2025-02-20 - Marta Lopez (Solutions): Suggested adding 'burst budget burn-down' visualization to Console so customers can see remaining burst allowance; PM to add as a follow-up (separate ticket).

2025-02-24 - Daniel Kim: Drafted ranking rules for triage: map to SLA tiers using thresholds for p99, sustained tokens/minute, and sustained concurrency. Shared draft PRD link in attachments. Engineering to validate with historical workload traces.

2025-02-27 - Asha Patel: Small pilot with Acme Corp scheduled; they provided sample traffic for sizing. Pilot will validate burst-to-reserved ratio assumptions. Added customer_impact flag 'high' to reflect sales urgency.

2025-03-01 - Daniel Kim: Incorporated pilot feedback: Acme needed 6x burst for 30s windows during nightly batch ops — we recommended a burst-queueing fallback and a paid-burst add-on rather than expanding reserved pools. Updated decisions accordingly.
